quark_ponders.ponder.minecraft_chain.tex: Chains can now connect blocks together when a piston moves them
As you can see, the chain block itself doesn't have to be moved by the piston, and will attach indirectly to other moved blocks.
Chains will only connect to blocks if they do so §9visually.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_1:
The Chute is a new automation block.
§9This is §4NOT§9 a hopper!
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_2: Items can be inserted into it via automation (§9Hopper, Dropper, etc§f)
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_3: Any items inserted are instantly dropped under it, always precisely in the center.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_4: The Chute can be disabled with a §4redstone§f signal..
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_5: Placing a block under it disables it too.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_chute.text_6:
The Chute can drop items through hollow logs.
(§9Any block with a hole in the middle§f)
quark_ponders.ponder.minecraft_dispenser: Dispensers are allowed to place blocks in the world.
Any blocks that already had a placement behaviour, like §4TNT§f, are ignored.
The blocks are rotated so they're placed §9forward§f from the dispenser.
Note that crops such as wheat seeds or potatoes also count.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_ender_watcher: The Ender Watcher is a new §4redstone§f input block.
It emits a §4redstone§f signal if a §3player§f is looking directly at it.
The signal is §4higher§f the closer to the center of the block the §3player§f is looking.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_feeding_troug: The Feeding Trough is a new block that can hold animal food in it.
While holding the correct food, it will attract and breed animals from §4%s§f blocks around it.
There's a chance the animal will need more than one bit of food to get in love mode.
If there's more than §4%s§f animals in a §4%d§f block radius, the animals will eat, but never enter love mode.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_gravisand.tex:
Gravisand is a new sand variant.
It will not fall unless primed with §4redstone§f.
However, if gravisand receives a signal, and can not fall, it'll instead float up.
Gravisand will propagate the signal to any adjacent gravisand blocks, causing them to fall or float as well.
Gravisand always outputs a comparator signal of §415§f.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_iron_rod.head: Iron Rod
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_iron_rod.text: Pistons pushing an Iron Rod will have it work as a drill of sorts.
An Iron Rod will §cbreak§f most blocks in front of it.
Iron Rods will only break blocks that pistons can push.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_metal_buttons: Gold and Iron buttons draw influence from Weighted Pressure Plates.

Gold Buttons emit a very short pulse.
(2 §4redstone§f ticks)

Iron Buttons emit a very long pulse.
(5 seconds)
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_obsidian_pres: Pressure Plates made with obsidian will only trigger when §3players§f walk over them.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_piston_move_t:
Pistons are allowed to move §cTile §cEntities§f.
(Blocks with extra data attached, like §aChests§f or §aFurnaces§f)
Attempting to move a block to an invalid position will cause it to §cbreak§f and drop its contents
For a block that pistons can't move, now that furnaces can't be used, look into §aSturdy §aStone§f in the §aBuilding§f category.
Note that some blocks such as §cMonster §cSpawners§f can't be moved this way, so you don't go and break the game!
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_§4redstone§f_: The Randomizer is a new §4redstone§f component.
When given a §4redstone§f signal from the back, it'll §crandomly§f enable either the left or right output.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_glass_item_fr: Glass Item Frames work like normal item frames but they hide when you place an item on them.
If you put a banner inside a §aGlass §aItem §aFrame§f, it'll sit flat with the wall with the pattern that's in it.
Glass Item Frames can attach to the front of a §aSign§f that's placed on the floor.
This will make the item show flush with the sign.
Glass Item Frames can be right clicked through to §aopen§f chests or other inventories.
When a map is placed in a Glass Item Frame, it will §aupdate §ain §areal §atime§f. Perfect for spies!
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_1: The Iron Grate a new block that lets §aitems§f fall through, but §cnot §cmobs§f.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_2: Additionally, farm mobs won't try to walk over them.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_3: Farm mobs on a leash are not affected!
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_grate.text_4: The Iron Grate can be waterlogged, items will float through it.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_1: The Rope can be placed on the bottom face of a block, by §3players§f and dispensers.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_2: You can also extend it down by right clicking the rope block with §amore §arope§f or dispenser.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_3: Right clicking with an empty hand or a §cnon §crope§f item will pull the rope up.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_4: But you §ccan't§f do it with dispensers!.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_rope.text_5: As you can see, ropes can pull up and push down (some) blocks at the end of them.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_1: Stools will §abounce§f you if you fall on them, like beds.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_2: And of course, you can sit on them.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_3: A §3player§f sitting on a stool will be §amoved§f with it when pulled/pushed with a piston.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_stool.text_4: Additionally, you can place blocks over them, which makes them get bigger, like a table.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_toretoise.tex: Oretoises are new neutral mobs that will spawn deep underground and in complete darkness.

When an Oretoise spawns, it'll come with a §9random§f type of ore.
(§aCoal§f, §aCopper§f, §aIron§f, §aLapis§f, or §aredstone§f).
You may attack the Oretoise with a pickaxe to have it drop that raw ore!
While §dSilk §dTouch§f makes it drop the ore block.
If you hit an Oretoise without a pickaxe, or when it has no ore, it'll emit a shockwave attack.
This will damage any non-Oretoise entities around, and redirect their aggro to you.
With enough care, it's possible to carry an Oretoise home and feed it so it grows more ores.
You can't boat or leash them.
But instead you can transport them in §aminecarts§f.
Feeding the Oretoise §aGlow §aBerries§f will sometimes have it regenerate its ores.
The Oretoise will regenerate a random ore each time.
You can use the §aFeeding §aTrough§f to feed them and regen the ores
When an Oretoise generates ore, it will enter an eating cooldown for §4%s§r seconds.
Oretoises are §a1§f block tall, but grow to §a1.4§f blocks tall if they have an ore.
Pushing an Iron Rod onto an Oretoise with a piston will break its ore.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_foxhound.head: Foxhound
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_foxhound.text: Foxhounds are new §chostile§f mobs that spawn in the Nether.
These fierce doggos will §cattack§f you and set you on §cfire§f..
If you're brave enough, drink a §6fire §6resistance§f potion and feed them some Coal to tame them.
It will ONLY work if you have the §6fire §6resistance§f effect.
Once tamed, they will work basically like wolves, but!..
They will sleep on hot blocks (like §amagma or §alit §afurnaces§f)
A foxhound on top of a furnace will §aspeed §aup§f the burning speed.
You can't put multiple doggos on a furnace to speed it up more, though.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_skull_spike.t: Setting a §aSkeleton §aSkull, §aZombie §aHead, or §aCreeper §aHead§f over a fence, will create a skull pike.
Nearby monsters in a §4%s§f block range and with line of sight will notice it, and run away in cowardice.
Note that Wither Skulls and Dragon head don't work for this.
Bosses and raiders are slightly more astute, and won't fall for this trickery.
Lastly, mobs focused on the §3player§f may not fear the spikes.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_enhanced_ladd: Right clicking a ladder with another one will place it, allowing you to drop ladders down without risking falling to your death.
As long as the first ladder is supported, the ones below can freestand.
When on a ladder, looking down will make you slide down the ladder very quickly.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_scaffolding_s: Right clicking on a Scaffold with a §ablock§f will attempt to place the block at the end of the Scaffold chain.
By default it'll turn direction once, so it can build blocks horizontally if you extend scaffolds that way.
If you wish to use the default behaviour of placing blocks on the scaffold, you can still do it with §cshift-right §cclick§f.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_slimes_to_mag: When a §alarge §aslime§f dies on §cmagma §cblocks§f, the §aslimes§f spawned will be turned into §cmagma §ccubes§f.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_1: Copper Pipes can transport items from point §aA§f to point §cB§f.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_2: To get items into a pipe simply use a §aHopper§f, §aDropper§f, or any other §ainsertion§f means you may have handy.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_3: At an intersection, Items will move §aforward§f if possible.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_4: If not, items will try to §arandomly§f flow left or right if possible.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_5:
Pipes can be disabled with §4redstone§f.
Items will not flow into disabled (§4powered§f) pipes.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_6: When items can't go any other direction, they will try go §aup§f.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_7: By default, all items will try go §adown§f whenever possible.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_8: Items can go §ain§f and §dout§f of pipes.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_9:
§4Comparators§f can read how many items are in a pipe.
One §4redstone§f lever per stack of blocks inside the pipe.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_10: If there is more than §4%s§f stacks of items (or this amount of §adifferent§f items) in one pipe, this will §cbreak§f and drop the items in the world.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_pipe.text_11: Finally, you can encase pipes in glass (this is purely §acosmetic§f).
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_1:
Magnets can move §8metallic §8blocks§f.
A metallic block is defined as block made out of §7Iron§f or §6Copper§f..
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_5: When multiple Magnets are exerting force upon the same block, the one with the §abiggest§f force wins.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_6: A magnet's force upon a block is the §4redstone§f level applied to it, minus the distance.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_7: Entities that are made of (or wearing) §amagnetic§f materials are also affected by magnets.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_8: When a Hopper is moved, it'll drop one of its items directly in front of it.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_9: If this item is a seed, it'll plant it either directly in front or one block down.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_magnet.text_1: When a Stonecutter is moved, it'll break any block that's above it%s
Very hard blocks such as §5Obsidian§f can't be broken like this.
When an Iron Rod is moved, it'll break any block that's in front of it.
Very hard blocks such as §5Obsidian§f can't be broken like this.
quark_ponders.ponder.quark_influence.tex: §cLit§f candles can influence the enchantments that appear in the Matrix Enchanter, up to a §4%s%%§f!
Each color Candle influence a different set of enchantments, check your Recipe Viewer to see which ones
For example, this §aLime Candle§f influences §9§o%s§f to appear%s
This §5inverts§f the effect of the candles, changing the influence to §dlower§f the possibility of those enchants to appear.
They will also become §5soul §5candles§f if the soul block is below the bookshelves!.
lit candles give the §asame §aamount§f of enchanting power as a bookshelf..
This configuration still provides §amax §aenchanting §apower§f for example.
